extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and advanced undergraduates studying algebraic geometry / sheaf theory
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, basic properties, and examples of presheaves and sheaves on a topological space; stalks/germs, sheaf axioms (identity and gluability), morphisms, sheafification, and related constructions. Includes exercises and motivating examples for students learning sheaf theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presheaf data
rubrics_metrics.description: A presheaf F on a topological space X assigns to each open set U ⊂ X a set F(U) (the sections over U), and for each inclusion U ⊂ V a restriction map resV,U : F(V) → F(U).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The data must satisfy resU,U = idF(U) and composition compatibility: if U ⊂ V ⊂ W then resW,U = resV,U ∘ resW,V. Notational variants F(U)=Γ(U,F)=H^0(U,F) are common. (See §2.2.2.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Presheaf as a contravariant functor
rubrics_metrics.description: A presheaf is equivalent to a contravariant functor from the category of open sets of X (with inclusions as morphisms) to the target category (e.g., Sets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This viewpoint is useful for abstract reasoning (Exercise 2.2.A). It explains restriction maps and naturality of morphisms of presheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections and global sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements of F(U) are called sections of F over U. If the 'U' is omitted it is implicitly X, so 'sections of F' means global sections F(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the word 'section' in mind when thinking about sheaves arising from maps (see Exercise 2.2.G(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stalk / germ at a point
rubrics_metrics.description: The stalk F_p is the set of germs at p, defined as equivalence classes of pairs (f, U) with p ∈ U and f ∈ F(U), where (f,U) ~ (g,V) iff they agree on some neighborhood W ⊂ U∩V of p. Equivalently, F_p is the colimit lim_{p∈U} F(U).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Germs are 'shreds' of sections near p. The colimit description emphasizes filteredness and is useful for categorical arguments (see §2.2.4–2.2.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaf identity axiom (separated presheaf)
rubrics_metrics.description: If {U_i} covers U and f1, f2 ∈ F(U) satisfy resU,Ui f1 = resU,Ui f2 for all i, then f1 = f2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A presheaf satisfying just this is called a separated presheaf. Interpretationally: 'at most one way to glue.' Appears as first sheaf axiom in §2.2.6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaf gluability axiom
rubrics_metrics.description: If {U_i} covers U and given sections f_i ∈ F(U_i) which agree on pairwise overlaps (resUi,Ui∩Uj f_i = resUj,Ui∩Uj f_j for all i,j), then there exists f ∈ F(U) with resU,Ui f = f_i for all i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the existence part: 'at least one way to glue.' Together with identity axiom it characterizes sheaves (see §2.2.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Empty-set / final-object axiom (optional formulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some expositions include the axiom that F(∅) is a one-element set (the final object).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condition actually follows from the identity and gluability axioms in many contexts and is discussed as an oft-included but redundant axiom in §2.2.6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples: sheaves of functions (differentiable/continuous/smooth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include sheaves of differentiable functions, continuous functions, smooth functions, and plain functions: assigning the set of such functions on each open set with restriction being restriction of functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concrete examples motivate the axioms: sections are local functions that glue when compatible (motivating text in §2.1 and Exercise 2.2.D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Skyscraper sheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: Given p∈X and a set S, define i_{p,*} S by i_{p,*}S(U) = S if p∈U and {e} (a one-element set) if p∉U; this forms a sheaf (skyscraper sheaf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informally pictured as a skyscraper at p; caution that the picture can mislead about which stalks are nontrivial (see §2.2.9). Also generalizes to values in other categories with final object at ∅.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant presheaf vs constant sheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: The constant presheaf Spre has Spre(U)=S for all U (identity restriction maps) and need not be a sheaf. The constant sheaf associates locally constant maps to S (or maps to S with discrete topology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.2.E: Spre fails gluability in general; the constant sheaf (locally constant functions) is the sheafification of Spre. The distinction is important in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction of a sheaf to an open subset
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a sheaf on X and U ⊂ X is open, define the restriction F|_U by F|_U(V)=F(V) for V ⊂ U; this is a sheaf on U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for local constructions and is trivial but frequently used (Example 2.2.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Space of sections (espace étalé) construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a presheaf/sheaf F, form the disjoint union of all stalks with projection π: F → X and topologize so that subsets {(x, s_x): x∈U} coming from a section s∈F(U) are open; π is then a local homeomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This viewpoint gives geometric intuition, interprets pullback and sheafification, and can be used to construct the sheafification (see §2.2.11 and §2.4.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushforward (direct image) sheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: For a continuous map π: X → Y and a presheaf/sheaf F on X, define π_*F by (π_*F)(V) = F(π^{-1}(V)) for open V ⊂ Y. If F is a sheaf then π_*F is a sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pushforward is functorial π_* : Sets_X → Sets_Y (Exercise 2.3.B). There is a natural map on stalks relating (π_*F)_q and F_p when π(p)=q (Exercise 2.2.I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ringed spaces and O_X-modules
rubrics_metrics.description: If O_X is a sheaf of rings on X, then (X,O_X) is a ringed space. An O_X-module is a sheaf F of abelian groups such that for each U, F(U) is an O_X(U)-module and restriction maps respect the module action (the commutative diagram (2.2.13.1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generalizes modules and vector bundles: e.g., sheaf of differentiable sections of a vector bundle is an O_X-module (see §2.2.13–2.2.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of presheaves/sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism φ: F → G is a collection of maps φ(U): F(U) → G(U) for all opens U commuting with restriction maps (i.e., natural transformation of the functors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morphisms induce maps on stalks φ_p: F_p → G_p (Exercise 2.3.A). If two morphisms into a sheaf agree on stalks they are equal (Exercise 2.4.D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaf Hom (sheaf Mor)
rubrics_metrics.description: For sheaves F and G, define Hom(F,G)(U) := Mor(F|_U, G|_U); this assignment is a sheaf (often denoted Hom).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful: this is not Mor(F(U),G(U)). Hom behaves contravariantly in the first argument and covariantly in the second. Warning: Hom does not commute with taking stalks (see §2.3.C–2.3.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kernels and cokernels for (pre)sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: For φ: F → G a morphism of presheaves of abelian groups define ker^{pre}φ(U) = ker(φ(U)) and coker^{pre}φ(U)=coker(φ(U)). ker^{pre}φ is a presheaf and for morphisms of sheaves it is already a sheaf; coker^{pre}φ may fail to be a sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus kernels behave well at the presheaf level, but cokernels may require sheafification. Example in §2.3.J: presheaf of functions admitting a holomorphic logarithm gives a non-sheaf cokernel situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheafification and its universal property
rubrics_metrics.description: A sheafification of a presheaf F is a morphism sh: F → F^{sh} where F^{sh} is a sheaf and for any sheaf G and presheaf morphism g: F → G there exists a unique sheaf morphism f: F^{sh} → G making the diagram commute (Definition 2.4.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: F^{sh}(U) = {compatible germs (f_p)_{p∈U} coming from local representatives}. Sheaﬁﬁcation is unique up to unique iso (Exercise 2.4.G), is a functor left adjoint to the forgetful functor (Exercise 2.4.L), and induces isomorphisms on stalks (Exercise 2.4.M).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections determined by germs
rubrics_metrics.description: For a sheaf F, the natural map F(U) → ∏_{p∈U} F_p (sending a section to its germs) is injective (Exercise 2.4.A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This uses the identity axiom; it can fail for presheaves (Exercise 2.4.F). It motivates the notion of support and compatibility of germs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of a section is closed
rubrics_metrics.description: For a sheaf (or separated presheaf) of abelian groups and a global section s, the support Supp(s):={p∈X : s_p ≠ 0 in F_p} is a closed subset of X (Definition and Exercise 2.4.2–2.4.B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support captures where the section 'lives' and relies on the stalk/germ perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties and isomorphisms checkable at stalks
rubrics_metrics.description: Many facts about sheaves can be checked at the level of stalks: sections are determined by germs, morphisms are determined by their action on stalks, and a morphism of sheaves is an isomorphism iff it induces isomorphisms on all stalks (Exercises 2.4.A, 2.4.D, 2.4.E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This local-to-global principle is a hallmark of sheaves; note these statements are false for general presheaves (Exercise 2.4.F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of monomorphisms / subsheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: For a morphism φ: F → G of sheaves of sets, the following are equivalent: (a) φ is a monomorphism in the category of sheaves; (b) φ is injective on stalks φ_p: F_p → G_p for all p; (c) φ(U): F(U) → G(U) is injective for all open U (Exercise 2.4.N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives several equivalent concrete checks for injectivity/monomorphism for sheaf maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abelian-category behavior of (pre)sheaves of abelian groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Presheaves of abelian groups form an abelian category: one can form kernels, cokernels, images, quotients 'open set by open set', and exactness can be checked on opens. Sheaves of abelian groups form an additive category and later an abelian category after sheafification considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructions are pointwise on opens, but cokernels may require sheafification; see §2.3.5 and following exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equalizer/exact-sequence interpretation of sheaf axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: The identity and gluability axioms can be interpreted as exactness of an 'equalizer exact sequence' F(U) → ∏_i F(U_i) ⇒ ∏_{i,j} F(U_i ∩ U_j) for a cover {U_i} of U (Remark in §2.2.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This interpretation places the sheaf axioms in the language of exactness, useful for categorical/homological perspectives.
